text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Algerian expatriates in France to start voting on June 2, three days ahead of the parliamentary polling in Algeria. The Algerian voting in France, due to begin on June 1, was put back because of the French snap election being held on that day.

- Algerian officials say they were surprised by British Airways protest at the resumption of operations by Air Algerie in Paris when the British company had said nothing in London where the Algerian airline is operating. French Versailles court, declaring itself geographically incompetent, sent British Airways to Melun court on Tuesday to pursue its bid to win tighter security at Paris's Charles de Gaulle airport.

- More than 40 countries agree to send officials to monitor Algeria's general elections. The observers will work within a U.N. team. The Organisation for African Unity and Arab League are also sending observers.

- President Liamine Zeroual, meeting human rights observatory officials, reasserts that individual and civic human rights are guaranteed by Algeria law and insists on the need to respect and promote citizens' social, cultural and economic rights.
- Abdallah Djaballah, leader of the Islamist-oriented Nahda party, says the June elections are a meaningful opportunity to further stability and democracy.
- Independent poll watchdog and the authorities begin checking the validity of candidates who have registered to compete in the June 5 general election.

- The Workers' Union celebrates May Day in the absence of its charismatic leader Abdelhaq Benhamouda, killed early this year by Moslem rebels, and amid economic reforms threating many jobs and purchasing power.
